answer: One concrete defense ties reward eligibility to a bond that must be re-locked each epoch and is slashed when a random peer-audit panel catches collusion. Picture each identity as a sparrow forced to carry its own nectar — a non-transferable deposit — before it can reach the reward zenith. A farm of N fakes must fund N full bonds up front and keep every one passing surprise audits, so cost scales linearly with headcount while an honest node pays just once; a single failed audit forfeits that identity's stake, making the attack strictly loss-making.
